awarding_org: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
funder_current_name: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
funding_share_basis: Origin: the IRE created and paid for the medal itself on 15 February 1917 out of its own society funds - ETHW's history says 'the IRE established its own medal' and names no donor, bequest, or endowment. Today: the purse is US$2,000,000 (from the 2025 medal; US$50,000 before), and it is IEEE's own money. IEEE's award record for the Medal of Honor now shows a single sponsor logo linking to ieee.org (not to the Foundation), IEEE Spectrum's 2025 laureate announcement states 'IEEE sponsors the annual award', the increase was approved by the IEEE Board of Directors, and IEEE's own FAQ justifies it by 'IEEE's role as a public charity' while naming no donor. The IEEE Foundation, IEEE's captive 501(c)(3), was named as sponsor in older IEEE listings and still supports many IEEE medals, but it cannot be supplying most of this purse: its 2025 audited statements report total 'Recognition awards' expense of US$2,033,987 across the entire IEEE awards portfolio, with the Energize/Recognition of Innovation pillar totalling US$1,485,294 (2024: US$1,653,227), and its schedule of named funds lists no Medal of Honor fund (it does list e.g. an IEEE James Maxwell Medal Fund). So any Foundation donor money is well under 50% of the US$2M, and the majority is IEEE parent funds. Because IEEE is the IRE's legal successor (1963 merger with the AIEE), today's purse is the same source of money as at origin - the awarding society's own funds - so most of today's purse is not new outside money.
money_note: US$2 million, shared equally among up to three recipients, effective with the 2025 medal (previously US$50,000); paid by IEEE itself following a 2024 IEEE Board of Directors decision, with no external donor or dedicated endowment named.
status_note: Established 1917 as the IRE Medal of Honor; renamed the IEEE Medal of Honor after the IRE merged with the AIEE to form IEEE in 1963. Not awarded in 1918, 1925, 1947, 1965, and 1976. Awarded continuously since; 2025 to Henry Samueli and 2026 to Jensen Huang.
judgment_reason: The alternative is to keep the current funder as the IEEE Foundation (Philanthropy) and code funder_changed true, since IEEE's older recipient-list PDF says 'The IEEE Medal of Honor is sponsored by the IEEE Foundation' and the Foundation is a legally separate donor-funded body. We rejected that because the Foundation's entire 2025 recognition-award spending across all IEEE medals (US$1.18-1.49M) is smaller than this one purse, it holds no Medal of Honor fund, and IEEE's current award page and Spectrum name IEEE itself as sponsor - so the >50%-of-the-money test puts today's purse on IEEE's own funds, the same society money (via the IRE-to-IEEE succession) that founded the medal in 1917.
